security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives from Markdown documentation, Telegram API examples, placeholders, or parser noise. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malicious command execution, or obfuscated payloads in the cited files. The skill still handles sensitive Telegram development topics, so production examples should stress secret management, privacy, and validation.

remediation.issue: Code samples contain placeholder tokens and API credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning beside each credential placeholder to use environment variables or a secret manager.

remediation.issue: Sensor, location, payment, and storage examples need privacy context.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, retention, validation, and least privilege notes near those examples.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static command-execution heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as reference snippets and avoid ambiguous fenced blocks when possible.

content.user_title: Build Telegram Bots and Mini Apps
content.value_statement: Telegram development spans bots, Mini Apps, webhooks, payments, and MTProto clients. This skill provides focused guides, templates, and best practices for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bot API basics, long polling, webhook setup, and common message operations.
Provides Python examples for messages, callbacks, inline queries, and webhooks.
Covers Mini App setup, UI controls, storage, sensors, payments, and initData validation.
Includes keyboard and button templates for python-telegram-bot and Telethon.
Lists official Telegram docs, repositories, libraries, and setup resources.
Summarizes TDLib and MTProto client development requirements.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not a deployed bot or runtime service.
Code examples use placeholders and need production security review.
Users should verify current Telegram API behavior in official docs.
It does not provide automated testing, hosting, or credential management.

use_cases.title: Ship a Support Bot
use_cases.description: Plan a Telegram support bot with messages, buttons, callbacks, and webhook deployment.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Mini App
use_cases.description: Design an in-app Telegram experience with WebApp controls, storage, payments, and validation.

use_cases.title: Plan Client Integrations
use_cases.description: Compare Bot API, Mini Apps, MTProto, and TDLib before choosing an integration path.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to outline a beginner Telegram bot. Include BotFather setup, token handling, long polling, and a first reply flow.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interactive Buttons
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to design a button flow for my Telegram bot. Cover inline buttons, reply keyboards, callbacks, and user permission checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Mini App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to plan a Telegram Mini App. Include WebApp initialization, theme handling, storage choices, payments, and initData validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-dev to review a production Telegram system. Cover webhooks, validation, rate limits, deployment, payments, privacy, and MTProto tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: I need a Telegram bot with callback buttons for account settings.
output: Recommended flow: start command, settings menu, callback handlers, permission checks, and confirmation messages.
The response explains which Telegram APIs to use and where to validate user identity.

output_examples.input: Help me plan a Telegram Mini App checkout experience.
output: The skill outlines WebApp launch methods, invoice handling, payment status states, and server-side initData validation.
It also flags HTTPS, token storage, and privacy requirements before production use.

output_examples.input: Should I use Bot API, Mini Apps, or MTProto for this product?
output: The answer compares integration scope, authentication needs, platform limits, and operational complexity.
It recommends a path based on user workflow, required Telegram features, and maintenance cost.

best_practices: Store bot tokens, API hashes, and payment secrets outside source control.
Validate Telegram initData and all user actions on the server.
Use webhooks, rate limits, and structured error handling for production bots.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real bot tokens into prompts, examples, or repositories.
Do not trust Mini App client data without server-side validation.
Do not request sensors, location, or payments without clear user consent.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Telegram Bot API, Mini Apps, webhooks, keyboards, payments, storage, sensors, MTProto, and TDLib.

faq.question: Does it create a live bot automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance and templates that developers adapt in their own projects.

faq.question: Can it help with Telegram Mini Apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains WebApp setup, UI controls, launch methods, payments, storage, and initData validation.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes token handling, HTTPS, permission checks, server validation, and sensitive data cautions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I handle Telegram credentials?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a secret manager. Never commit real tokens, API hashes, or payment secrets.
